test/package-test.sh: 1
`90-90`: ** Trivial** · **Maintainability & Code Quality** · **Quick win** **Match the full patch-apply line instead of a substring.** Line 90 checks only that the substring `apply --recount --check` appears somewhere in the workflow. The check still passes in these cases: - The substring appears only in a comment. - The loop runs `--check` but no longer applies the patches. - The upstream fetch, checkout, or commit-verification lines are removed. Each of those changes silently weakens the pinned-upstream patch check. Assert the exact lines, as Lines 84-89 already do for the other inputs.
🛡️ Proposed fix
```diff - grep -Fq 'apply --recount --check' "$workflow" || fail "pinned-upstream patch checks missing" + grep -Fxq ' test "$(git -C "$src" rev-parse HEAD)" = "$commit"' "$workflow" || + fail "pinned-upstream commit verification missing" + grep -Fxq ' for p in patches/*.patch; do git -C "$src" apply --recount --check "$PWD/$p"; git -C "$src" apply --recount "$PWD/$p"; done' "$workflow" || + fail "pinned-upstream patch checks missing" ```
Based on learnings: "ensure the check asserts the exact required value ... rather than using a loose substring/count match."
